sections.about: Kinds of entity. The application declares each kind once; every query is built from it.

names.name: Kind
names.signature: (label: str, key: str = 'key', times: tuple[str, ...] = (), relations: dict = <factory>, text: tuple[str, ...] = (), dimensions: int = 0) -> None
names.doc:
A kind of entity, declared once by the application.

label      node label
key        property that identifies one entity
times      values that are stored as native time values
relations  {TYPE: Kind}: edges from this kind to another, each with a validity window.
           Use SELF for a relation to the same kind: `{"KNOWS": SELF}`
text       values that can be searched by their words
dimensions size of the vectors that stand for that text; 0 for no search by meaning

A Kind cannot change after it is made: its names were checked once and go into queries.

names.name: SELF
names.doc: = 'self'

sections.about:
Which graph holds what, the schema a graph needs before the first write, and the marks
that the engine keeps on a graph's stamp: the serial of the last entry stored, and how far
each job that reads entries off the write path has come.

names.name: WORLD
names.doc: = 'world'

names.name: ensure_schema
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kinds=(), wait_seconds: float = 10.0, entry_dimensions: int = 0) -> None
names.doc:
Create a unique constraint on the key of every kind, a full-text index on the text
of every kind and of its States, a vector index for every kind with dimensions, and the
engine's own indexes, among them the full-text index of entries. With `entry_dimensions`,
entries get a vector index of that size too, for embed_entries() and nearest_entries(). Give the graph its stamp, once.
A duplicate key then fails the whole query. Safe to call on every start.

Call it before the first write. When it adds a kind to a graph that is in use, stop
the writers first: a write during the build of an index is lost from that index.

names.name: tenant
names.signature: (db: falkordb.falkordb.FalkorDB, tenant_id: str) -> falkordb.graph.Graph
names.doc:
The private graph of one tenant. FalkorDB accepts any graph name, so the identifier
is checked here: a tenant can never name the world graph or another tenant's graph.

names.name: world
names.signature: (db: falkordb.falkordb.FalkorDB) -> falkordb.graph.Graph
names.doc: The graph every tenant may read.

sections.about: The write path: rows become versions. No LLM is involved.

names.name: record_failure
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, reason: str, kind: str | None = None, key=None, detail=None, owner=None)
names.doc:
Store a write that did not happen, so it is never lost silently.

What is stored is bounded and safe, whatever the refused write held: `detail` is cut to
2,000 characters, and a kind or key that is not a valid one is left out. `owner` names
the user whose content the refused write held, so that it can be erased with the rest.

names.name: remember
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, rows, by: str) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
Store what is true about entities of one kind, from the time `t` of each row.

A row is {"key", "t", "values", "relations", "entry"}; key and t are required.
  values     properties of the entity. Null or missing means the value is absent.
  relations  {TYPE: key or list of keys} of the entities it points at, for the types
             declared in the Kind. Missing means it points at none.
  entry      the id of the entry the row comes from, such as an observation. A State
             that the row adds points at that entry, as its evidence.
A row is the full picture at time t: what it does not name is no longer true.
`by` names the agent or source that writes. It is stored on every State and edge.

Returns one receipt per row, in order: {"key", "status"} with status
  created    first State of the entity
  changed    the row differs: the current State is closed and a new one added
  inserted   the row came late: it is put into the history at its time
  unchanged  the row is already recorded for that time
  stale      the row came late, after a row with a later time that repeated what held
             before it: where it ends is not known, so it is refused
  conflict   another row with other content has the same time: refused
  missing    the entry it names does not exist: refused
  invalid    the row cannot be stored
  failed     the database refused the query
Stale, conflicting, missing, invalid, and failed rows leave a WriteFailure node.

names.name: update
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, key, t, by: str, values=None, relations=None, entry=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Change the values and relations it names, from time `t` on. A value of None removes
it. A relation that it names gets the targets it gives, and keeps none other. The rest
stays as the current State says. An entity that does not exist starts with what the
update names.

Returns a receipt as remember() does. Besides, it can say
  stale  `t` is before the current State: an update changes what is current. Send the
         full row of that time to remember() instead.
  busy   other writers changed the entity each time it was read: refused

sections.about: Reads of what was true: the versions of an entity, and its state at any time.

names.name: as_of
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, key, when) -> dict | None
names.doc: The State that was valid at `when`, or None if the entity was not known then.

names.name: history
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, key) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
Every State of an entity, oldest first. A State that a row with an entry added has
"entry": the id of that entry.

names.name: related
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, key, relation: str, when=None) -> list
names.doc: Keys of the entities that `key` pointed at through `relation` at `when` (default: now).

sections.about:
Recall: finding what is in memory, by the graph around an entity, by the words of its
text now and earlier, by the words of entries, and by the meaning of its text and of entries.

names.name: embed
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, embedder, model: str, limit: int = 100) -> dict
names.doc:
Give a vector to entities of `kind` whose text has none, or whose text or model has
changed since. At most `limit` in one call. Returns {"embedded", "waiting"}: how many
got a vector now, and how many still wait. Run it off the write path until none wait.

`embedder` takes a list of texts and returns one vector for each, of kind.dimensions
numbers. `model` names what made them. A call with another model than the last one
reads the kind once, to give every entity with text a vector of the new model.

names.name: embed_entries
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, embedder, model: str, limit: int = 100) -> dict
names.doc:
Give a vector to entries whose text has none of this model, at most `limit` in one
call, in the order they were stored. Returns {"embedded", "waiting"}, as embed() does.
Run it off the write path until none wait.

It reads the entries stored since its mark for this model: a model it has not seen
starts from the first entry.

names.name: fuse
names.signature: (rankings: dict[str, list[dict]], limit: int = 10) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
Merge rankings of the same kind of entity, best first:
[{"key", "score", "places"}]. `rankings` maps a name to the result of similar(),
search(), or nearest(). "places" maps each ranking's name to the place it gave the
entity, from 1.

names.name: nearest
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, question: str, embedder, model: str, limit: int = 10) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
Entities of `kind` whose text is closest in meaning to `question`, closest first:
[{"key", "score", "values"}]. The score is the cosine similarity: 1 for the same
direction, 0 for none in common.

An entity whose text changed after its vector was made is left out until embed() runs
again. So is a vector of another model. A question without text finds nothing.
At most 1,000 vectors are read: after a change of model, run embed() to the end first.

names.name: nearest_entries
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, question: str, embedder, model: str, limit: int = 10) -> list
names.doc:
Entries whose text is closest in meaning to `question`, closest first:
[{"id", "score", "entry"}], with the score as nearest() gives it. Vectors of another
model are left out, and at most 1,000 vectors are read.

names.name: pointing_at
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, relation: str, key, when=None) -> list
names.doc:
Keys of the entities of `kind` whose `relation` pointed at `key` at `when` (default:
now). The reverse of related(): related() asks where one entity points, this asks what
points at one target.

names.name: search
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, question: str, limit: int = 10, match: str = 'all') -> list[dict]
names.doc:
Entities of `kind` whose text has the words of `question`, best first:
[{"key", "score", "values"}]. "values" holds the current values of the entity.

  match  "all": every word must be there. "any": one word is enough.

Words are matched whole and in their base form: "sensors" finds "sensor". A question
without a letter or digit finds nothing.

names.name: search_entries
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, question: str, limit: int = 10, match: str = 'all') -> list[dict]
names.doc:
Entries of episodes whose values had the words of `question`, best first:
[{"id", "score", "entry"}]. "entry" holds the properties of the entry, as episode()
gives them, without its evidence.

names.name: search_history
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, question: str, limit: int = 10, match: str = 'all') -> list[dict]
names.doc:
States of entities of `kind` whose text had the words of `question`, the current one
or an earlier one, best first: [{"key", "score", "state"}]. "state" is the State as
history() gives it, with its validity window.

Words are matched as search() matches them.

names.name: similar
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, key, relations=None, limit: int = 10) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
Entities of the same kind that share relation targets with this one, most shared
first: [{"key", "shared", "through"}]. "through" lists what is shared, as
(relation, key of the target), so the reason can be shown.

This entity's current relations are compared with every relation the others ever had,
so entities of the past are found. `relations` narrows the relations that count.

sections.about: Episodes: the ordered record of one event, written by agents.

names.name: close_episode
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, episode_id: str, by: str, outcome=None, cites=(), at=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Record what the event ended in, and close the episode. The outcome is the last entry.
Returns the same receipt as record().

names.name: episode
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, episode_id: str) -> dict | None
names.doc:
An episode with its entries in order, or None if it does not exist. Each entry has
"cites": the (label, key) pairs it rests on. "about" has the same form.

names.name: episodes_about
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, key) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
The episodes about one entity, newest first. Each has "outcome": the entry that
closed it, or None while it is open.

names.name: open_episode
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, episode_id: str, by: str, about=(), at=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Start the record of one event. `about` lists the entities it concerns, as (Kind, key).

Returns a receipt {"id", "status"} with status
  opened   the episode was made
  exists   an episode with this id is there already; nothing changed
  missing  an entity in `about` does not exist: refused
  invalid  `about` or `at` cannot be used: refused
  failed   the database refused the query
Missing, invalid, and failed leave a WriteFailure node.

names.name: record
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, episode_id: str, entry_type: str, by: str, values=None, cites=(), at=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Append one entry to an episode: an observation, a forecast, an action, or any other
type the application names.

  values  properties of the entry
  cites   the evidence: ids of earlier entries, entities as (Kind, key), and other
          episodes as ("Episode", id)
  at      when it happened (default: now)

Returns a receipt. {"id", "seq", "status": "recorded"} when stored. Otherwise
{"id": None, "status", "reason"} with status
  unknown  the episode does not exist
  closed   the episode is closed
  full     the episode has 5,000 entries
  missing  something in `cites` does not exist
  invalid  `values`, `cites`, or `at` cannot be stored
  failed   the database refused the query
and a WriteFailure node that holds the refused entry.

sections.about: The free-text path: what agents wrote in entries becomes rows, off the write path.

names.name: extract
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, extractor, by: str, types=None, limit: int = 100) -> dict
names.doc:
Read entries with text that were not read for `kind` yet, in the order they were
stored, at most `limit` of them, and write the rows that `extractor` finds in each.

  extractor  a function of one entry (its properties: id, type, at, by, and its values)
             that returns a list of rows of `kind`, as remember() takes them. A row
             without "t" is true from the time of the entry. Its "entry" is the entry.
  types      the types of entries to read, such as ["observation"] (default: all)

Returns {"read", "rows", "waiting"}: how many entries were read, how many rows came back
with each status of remember(), and how many entries still wait. An extractor that
raises stops the call; the entry it read stays waiting, and the ones before it are done.

sections.about: Handoffs: one agent passes work to another by pointing at what the other must read.

names.name: accept
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, handoff_id: str, by: str) -> dict
names.doc:
Take a handoff. Returns a receipt {"id", "status"} with status
  accepted  the handoff is now accepted by the agent it was given to
  exists    that agent accepted it before; nothing changed
  refused   it was given to another agent
  unknown   there is no such handoff
Refused and unknown leave a WriteFailure node that names who tried.

names.name: hand_off
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, handoff_id: str, by: str, to: str, points_to, values=None, at=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Pass work from agent `by` to agent `to`.

  points_to  what the receiver must read: entry ids, ("Episode", id), and entities as
             (Kind, key). At least one. An entity is pinned to the time of the handoff.
  values     short properties of the handoff, such as what is asked
  at         when it was given (default: now)

Returns a receipt {"id", "status"} with status
  given    the handoff was made
  exists   a handoff with this id is there already; nothing changed
  missing  something in `points_to` does not exist: refused
  invalid  it points at nothing, or the values, references, or time cannot be stored
  failed   the database refused the query
Missing, invalid, and failed leave a WriteFailure node that holds the refused handoff.

names.name: handoffs_for
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, agent: str, waiting_only: bool = True) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
What was handed to an agent, oldest first. Each has "points_to": the (label, key)
pairs to read. By default only the handoffs the agent has not accepted yet.

sections.about: Lessons: what was learned from episodes that ended. The semantic memory.

names.name: learn
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, lesson_id: str, by: str, statement: str, supported_by, about=(), values=None, at=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Store what was learned, with the episodes it was learned from.

  statement     the lesson, in words
  supported_by  ids of episodes that have ended. At least one.
  about         the entities it is about, as (Kind, key)
  values        other properties of the lesson

Returns a receipt {"id", "status"} with status
  learned  the lesson was stored
  exists   a lesson with this id is there already; nothing changed
  missing  an episode has not ended or does not exist, or an entity does not exist
  invalid  no statement, no episode, or something that cannot be stored
  failed   the database refused the query
Missing, invalid, and failed leave a WriteFailure node that holds the refused lesson.

names.name: lesson
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, lesson_id: str) -> dict | None
names.doc: A lesson with its weight, the episodes for and against it, and what it is about.

names.name: lessons_about
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, key, at_least: int = 1, since=None) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
The lessons about one entity that still hold, heaviest first. Each has "weight".

at_least  the least weight a lesson needs to be given out
since     leave out lessons that no episode has supported, contradicted, or used
          since this time: a lesson that nothing touches fades

names.name: retire
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, lesson_id: str, by: str, why: str, at=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Say that a lesson no longer holds. It stays in the graph with its evidence, and is no
longer given out. Status: retired, exists (it was retired before), or unknown.

names.name: used
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, lesson_id: str, by: str, episode_id: str, helped=None, at=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Record that a lesson was used in an episode. `helped` says whether acting on it led
to a correct result: True, False, or None while that is not known. It can be said once,
in this call or a later one. Status: used, judged, exists, or a refusal.

names.name: weigh
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, lesson_id: str, by: str, episode_id: str, agrees: bool, at=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Add an episode that ended as evidence for a lesson, or against it. An episode counts
once. Status: weighed, exists, or the refusals missing, retired, unknown.

sections.about: Playbooks: what to do when a situation comes again. The procedural memory.

names.name: playbook
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, name: str, version: int | None = None) -> dict | None
names.doc:
One version of a playbook with its trigger, steps, counts, and the episodes it rests
on. The newest version by default. None if there is none.

names.name: playbooks_for
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, situation: dict) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
The playbooks that are switched on and whose trigger fits a situation: every property
of the trigger is in the situation with the same value. Best record first: successes
minus failures, then runs.

names.name: ran
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, name: str, by: str, episode_id: str, succeeded=None, stop_after: int = 3, at=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Record that the newest version of a playbook ran in an episode. `succeeded` says how
it ended: True, False, or None while that is not known. It can be said once, in this
call or a later one. After `stop_after` failures in a row the playbook switches off.

Returns {"id", "status", "enabled"} with status recorded, judged, or exists; or a
refusal with status missing (the episode) or unknown (the playbook).

names.name: switch
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, name: str, by: str, on: bool) -> dict
names.doc:
Switch the newest version of a playbook on or off. Switching on clears the count of
failures in a row. Status: on, off, exists (it was so already), or unknown.

names.name: write_playbook
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, name: str, by: str, trigger, steps, supported_by, needs: int = 3, at=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Write the next version of a playbook. The version before it is switched off.

  trigger       the situation it is for: properties that must all be there
  steps         what to do, in order: a list of property maps
  supported_by  ids of the episodes it was drawn from. All must have ended.
  needs         how many episodes it must rest on (default 3)

Returns a receipt. {"id", "version", "status": "written"} when stored. Otherwise
{"id": None, "status", "reason"} with status
  missing      an episode in `supported_by` does not exist or has not ended
  unsupported  it rests on fewer episodes than it needs
  invalid      no trigger, no steps, or something that cannot be stored
  failed       the database refused the query
and a WriteFailure node that holds the refused playbook.

sections.about: Promotion: what repeats in episodes that ended becomes a lesson or a playbook.

names.name: promote
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, by: str, rule, at_least: int = 3) -> dict
names.doc:
Read every episode that ended, ask `rule` what each one shows, and write what that
adds up to. `at_least` is how many episodes must agree before a lesson is learned or a
playbook is written (default 3).

Returns {"episodes", "lessons", "playbooks", "runs"}: how many episodes were read, and
a receipt for each lesson, playbook, and run that a claim named. Besides the statuses
of the library, a receipt can say
  waiting    fewer episodes agree than `at_least`; "for" says how many do
  unchanged  nothing new: every episode is counted, or the playbook has these steps
A lesson that is learned or weighed says how many episodes were "new" to it.

sections.about:
Algorithms over the graph: what belongs together, what is central, and how two things
are connected.

names.name: between
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kinds, relations=None, limit: int = 10, sample: int | None = None, seed: int = 1, at=None) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
Entities by the shortest paths between other entities that run through them, highest
first: [{"entity": (label, key), "score"}]. The score is the number of such paths; where
several shortest paths join two entities, each counts for its part. Of equal scores,
the oldest entity comes first.

A path follows the direction of the relations. So an entity scores only when relations
lead into it and out of it: a relation from a kind to itself, or a chain of kinds. Where
one kind only points at another, every score is 0.

Paths are counted from `sample` entities picked at random, and the counts are scaled up
to all: an estimate, and the same one for the same `seed`. It finds the entities that
stand out; it cannot order entities whose scores are close. The count is exact when the
sample is as large as the number of entities. Without `sample`, it is as large as WORK
allows and at least SAMPLE, so a small graph gets the exact count.

With `at`, over the relations that held at that time. The paths are counted here, not in
FalkorDB: from fewer entities for the same work, picked by `seed` in another way.

names.name: connection
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, start, end, kinds=(), relations=None, max_hops: int = 6, at=None) -> list[dict] | None
names.doc:
The shortest chain of relations from `start` to `end`, as its steps in order. None
when no chain of up to `max_hops` steps joins them, or one of them is not known. The
same thing twice is no step: [].

start, end  references: (Kind, key) for an entity, (label, id) for a record
kinds       more kinds whose relations may be followed. The kinds of start and end,
            and every kind they point at, are followed already: name a kind that
            points at both
relations   the edge types to follow, in either direction. Default: every relation of
            those kinds. Name ABOUT, CITES, and the like to go through records as well

A step is {"from", "relation", "to", "forward", "current", "since", "until"}.
  from, to  (label, key) pairs in the order of the walk. The key is None for an entity
            of a kind that was not given
  forward   False when the relation points from "to" to "from"
  current   whether the relation holds now. "since" and "until" are the start and the
            end of the last time it held; "until" is None while it holds
Where several relations join the two things of a step, the step tells of one that holds
now, and if none does, of the one that ended last.

With `at`, the shortest chain of relations that held at that time, between entities.
A step tells of a relation that held then; "current" and "until" say whether it holds
now, and when it ended.

names.name: groups
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kinds, relations=None, records=(), at_least: int = 2, limit=100, show=100, at=None) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
Sets of things that are linked, directly or through other things, largest first:
[{"size", "members"}]. Two things are in one set when a chain of relations joins them,
whichever way the relations point.

kinds      the entities that take part: these kinds and every kind they point at
records    labels of records that take part too: Episode, Entry, Lesson, Playbook
relations  the edge types that link. Default: every relation of the kinds, and with
           records also what a record is about, has, cites, and rests on
at_least   the smallest set that is listed. 1 lists what is linked to nothing as well
"members" holds up to `show` members as (label, key) pairs, oldest first. Sets of one
size come in the order of their oldest members.

With records=["Episode"] and relations=["ABOUT"], a set holds the episodes that are
about the same entities, and those entities.

With `at`, the sets that the relations joined at that time, of the entities that existed
then. Records have no time: they cannot take part.

names.name: important
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, kinds, relation=None, limit: int = 10, at=None) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
Entities by PageRank, highest first: [{"entity": (label, key), "score"}]. Of equal
scores, the oldest entity comes first.

An entity scores high when many entities point at it, and higher when those score high
themselves. An entity shares its score evenly among what it points at; one that points
at nothing shares it among all.

The rank is taken over the entities of every kind and the edges of `relation` (default:
every relation), so the scores of all entities add up to 1. Entities of `kinds`, and of
the kinds they point at, are listed. With `at`, over the entities that existed and the
relations that held at that time.

sections.about: Causal blast-radius analysis and non-destructive entry invalidation.

names.name: impact_of_entry
names.signature: (graph, entry_id: str) -> dict | None
names.doc: Traces every downstream record that cited or derived from `entry_id`.

names.name: impact_of_state
names.signature: (graph, kind: lighthouse.kinds.Kind, key, since, until) -> dict
names.doc:
Finds every record that relied on `(kind, key)` during `[since, until)`.

Returns direct entries, transitive downstream entries, derived entity states,
affected episodes, waiting handoffs, and lessons or playbooks placed at risk.

names.name: invalidate_entry
names.signature: (graph, entry_id: str, by: str, reason: str, at=None) -> dict
names.doc: Marks an entry as retracted without deleting it and returns its blast radius.

sections.about: Temporal world diffing and zero-copy counterfactual simulation.

names.name: diff_between
names.signature: (graph, kinds, t1, t2) -> dict
names.doc: Computes the structural delta across `kinds` between `t1` and `t2`.

names.name: what_if
names.signature: (graph, kinds, hypothetical_rows: list[tuple[lighthouse.kinds.Kind, list[dict]]], at=None, situation=None) -> dict
names.doc: Simulates `hypothetical_rows` in memory without writing to the database.

sections.about: Trust in an agent, read from what the graph already records about its work.

names.name: agent_trust
names.signature: (graph, agent: str) -> dict
names.doc:
How far the work of `agent` held: the counts of each kind of evidence, and "score",
from 0 to 1, or None for an agent with no evidence. The name is checked like every
name; it is not looked up as anyone's identity.

sections.about: Conversations: what was said in the sessions of a user, in order.

names.name: context
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, user: str, session_id: str, last: int = 20) -> dict
names.doc:
What a model needs to go on with a session: {"summary", "upto", "messages", "waiting"}.

  summary   what the messages up to number "upto" come to, or None
  messages  the messages after those, oldest first, at most `last`
  waiting   how many messages are in neither. Above 0, it is time to sum up again

A session that the user does not have gives an empty context.

names.name: forget_session
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, user: str, session_id: str) -> dict
names.doc:
Delete one session of `user`: its messages, its summary, the references that nothing
else mentions, and what was kept of its refused messages.

Returns {"id", "status", "messages"}: status "forgotten" with the number of messages
that were deleted, or "unknown" when the user has no such session.

Messages that are said while this runs are deleted with the rest. One that is said
after the session is gone opens it again.

names.name: forget_user
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, user: str) -> dict
names.doc:
Delete everything `user` said in this graph: every session, as forget_session()
does, and what was kept of every refused message. Returns {"user", "sessions",
"messages"} with how many were deleted.

names.name: messages
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, user: str, session_id: str, last: int = 20, before=None) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
The last messages of a session of `user`, oldest first, at most `last` of them. Each
has "mentions": the (label, key) pairs it names. `before` is the number of a message:
the messages just before that one are given, to read further back.

A session that the user does not have gives nothing.

names.name: said
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, user: str, question: str, limit: int = 10, match: str = 'all') -> list[dict]
names.doc:
The messages in the sessions of `user` whose text has the words of `question`, best
first. Each has "score" and "mentions".

  match  "all": every word must be there. "any": one word is enough.

Only the letters and digits of the question are used. A question without any finds
nothing.

names.name: said_about
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, user: str, reference, limit: int = 20) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
The messages in the sessions of `user` that mention one thing, newest first.
`reference` is (Kind, key) for an entity, or (label, id) for a record.

names.name: say
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, user: str, session_id: str, role: str, text: str, by: str, mentions=(), values=None, at=None) -> dict
names.doc:
Add one message to a session of `user`. The first message opens the session.

  role      who speaks, as the application names it: the user, an agent, a tool
  by        the agent or user that wrote the message
  mentions  what the message is about: entities as (Kind, key), records as (label, id)
  values    more properties of the message
  at        when it was said (default: now)

Returns a receipt. {"id", "seq", "status": "said"} when stored: the id of the session
and the number of the message in it. Otherwise {"id": None, "status", "reason"} with
  invalid  the text, the mentions, the values, or the time cannot be stored
  failed   the database refused the query
and a WriteFailure node that holds the refused message.

names.name: sessions
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, user: str, limit: int = 20) -> list[dict]
names.doc:
The sessions of `user`, the one written to last first: [{"id", "opened_at",
"active_at", "messages"}]. "messages" is how many it holds.

names.name: summarize
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, user: str, session_id: str, text: str, upto: int, by: str) -> dict
names.doc:
Store what the messages of a session up to number `upto` come to. The text is the
application's: the library holds no model. A session has one summary, and a later one
takes its place.

Returns a receipt. {"id", "upto", "status": "summed"} when stored. Otherwise
{"id": None, "status", "reason"} with status
  unknown  the user has no such session
  stale    the summary that is there reaches further than `upto`
  invalid  the text cannot be stored, or `upto` is not the number of a message
  failed   the database refused the query
and a WriteFailure node that holds the refused summary.

sections.about: Tasks that agents hand to each other through the graph.

names.name: add_task
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, task_id: str, kind: str, ref=None, after=()) -> bool
names.doc:
Add an open task. `ref` is the key of the graph entity the task is about. `after`
lists the ids of tasks that must be done before this one can be claimed.

Returns False, and changes nothing, if a task with this id exists. Raises ValueError,
and adds nothing, if a task in `after` does not exist.

names.name: claim
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, agent: str, kind: str, lease: int | None = None) -> dict | None
names.doc:
Give the oldest free task of `kind` to `agent`: {"id", "kind", "ref", "until"}. None if
no task is free.

`lease` is how many seconds the claim holds (default: until it is done or released).
After that, another agent can claim the task, and the first can no longer complete it.
"until" is the time the lease runs out, or None.

names.name: complete
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, agent: str, task_id: str) -> bool
names.doc:
Mark a task done. Only its owner can, once; returns False otherwise. An owner whose
lease ran out can still complete the task while no other agent has claimed it.

names.name: release
names.signature: (graph: falkordb.graph.Graph, agent: str, task_id: str) -> bool
names.doc:
Give a claimed task back, open for another agent. Only its owner can; returns False
otherwise.

sections.about: Times in the one form the library sends to FalkorDB.

names.name: now
names.signature: () -> str

names.name: stamp
names.signature: (value: str | datetime.datetime | None) -> str | None
names.doc:
A time as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` in UTC, the form FalkorDB's localdatetime() parses.

FalkorDB keeps whole seconds, so fractions are dropped. A time without an offset is
taken as UTC. The client cannot send datetime parameters, so queries get this string.
